questions.q: What is the main advantage of 'reserved' pricing over 'pay-as-you-go'?
options: It offers a significant discount in exchange for a 1-3 year commitment
It can be reclaimed by the provider with little notice
It is only available for storage, never compute
It requires no payment at all
questions.explain: Reserved pricing trades a 1-3 year commitment for a significant discount, well suited to workloads known to run continuously.

questions.q: What is 'spot' (or low-priority) capacity best suited for?
options: Mission-critical production databases that can never go down
Batch jobs that can tolerate being interrupted, since the provider can reclaim this capacity with little notice
Long-term reserved workloads
Physical data center maintenance
questions.explain: Spot capacity is unused provider capacity sold at a steep discount, but the provider can reclaim it with little notice, so it fits interruption-tolerant batch work best.

questions.q: Why can a workload be cheap on compute but still produce a large bill?
options: Because storage is always free
Because data egress — traffic leaving the provider's network — is often billed and can be a hidden cost driver
Because compute is the only thing ever billed
Because reserved pricing always costs more than pay-as-you-go
questions.explain: A cloud bill sums several independently metered things, and data leaving the network (egress) is often billed even though incoming traffic usually isn't — making it an easy-to-miss cost driver.

questions.q: What does the Azure pricing calculator let you do?
options: Provision real resources directly from the estimate
Estimate the monthly cost of planned services before provisioning anything
Automatically patch a virtual machine's operating system
Replace the need for a shared responsibility model
questions.explain: The pricing calculator lets you pick services and configuration and see an estimated monthly cost, without deploying any actual resources.

questions.q: Why would an organization tag its cloud resources with labels like 'team' or 'environment'?
options: Tags are required for a resource to run at all
Tags let a provider's cost reports be broken down by who is actually responsible for each cost, instead of one opaque combined bill
Tags automatically reduce the price of a resource
Tags replace the need for a pricing calculator
questions.explain: Tags are key-value labels that let a combined bill be broken down by team or project, which matters once an organization has more than a handful of resources.
